title: A Generalized Doubly Robust Learning Framework for Debiasing Post-Click Conversion Rate Prediction

problem.claim: Post-click conversion rate prediction must address severe selection bias caused by user self-selection and system item-selection processes.

gap.claim: Existing doubly robust approaches may generalize poorly because propensity scores and imputation terms are estimated inaccurately in practice.

contributions.claim: A generalized learning framework unifies existing doubly robust methods and supports development of debiasing techniques for different application scenarios.
Two new doubly robust methods, DR-BIAS and DR-MSE, are proposed.
A tri-level joint learning optimization method and corresponding efficient training algorithm are proposed for DR-MSE in CVR prediction.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper explicitly distinguishes a generalized framework, two new doubly robust methods, and a novel tri-level joint learning optimization method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: DR-BIAS directly controls the bias of the doubly robust loss.
DR-MSE flexibly balances bias and variance and is reported to achieve better generalization performance.
Experiments on real-world and semi-synthetic datasets are reported to validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: CVR prediction is important for user-interest discovery and platform revenue.
Severe selection bias arises from user and system selection behavior.
Existing doubly robust approaches can suffer poor generalization from propensity-score and imputation errors.
The paper introduces a generalized framework, DR-BIAS, DR-MSE, and a tri-level optimization method with an efficient training algorithm.
Experiments on real-world and semi-synthetic datasets are reported as validating the proposed methods.

source_observation.claim: The reported generalization problem is linked to inaccurate propensity-score estimation and imputation errors.

interpretation.claim: Debiasing methods should account for both bias and the quality of nuisance-term estimation.

application.claim: When adapting doubly robust learning, evaluate whether the method controls bias while maintaining reliable propensity and imputation estimates.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these considerations transfer beyond the stated CVR prediction settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative results or dataset names.
The abstract does not specify the theoretical bounds or optimization details.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported effectiveness.
